I've had a sitting elected official call for the mass deportation of Indians and label me a "foreign occupier." I've watched a demonstrator tear an Indian flag apart while a crowd chanted hate. Every time, we're told it's rhetoric, it's just politics, it doesn't really mean anything. Tell that to a man recovering in a Wyoming hospital. Words from the government carry weight precisely because they come from the government. When DHS puts out an image mocking a man's name and his ability to drive because of what he looks like, it doesn't just offend people. It makes them targets. They put his name on a government post. He ended up in a hospital bed, stabbed 17 times. If there isn't a cost, then rhetoric like this will keep coming, and someone else will pay the price next. I am done accepting this as the price of doing politics in this country. Equal Opportunity Now exists to elect leaders who will make sure it isn't free — leaders who will call this out the moment it happens and fight to hold the people responsible accountable. = = | | | No American should have to fear for their life because of their name. — Raja Krishnamoorthi Founder | Equal Opportunity Now | = Equal Opportunity Now is d/b/a Reviving American Jobs Again PAC (RAJA PAC) Equal Opportunity Now P.O. This was the first election since the rollback of the legislation that ended Jim Crow, the Voting Rights Act, and voters made themselves heard. Voters defeated all five of the statewide amendments be
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LK9LNBKxC5PJmZtk9Qvhk3S0ZCL5-fzoodDygO4EHy9FgQ-U1qBfvA9X0x1Yl0VbIFI3Oc9gOI4YR7JfRsdml-FnnTSvDAyj1Bg_Xja6zusFq-ReUkqhRtrUI_IVUbqJS0S2Ce59044CDSM6wyjYbHMACiVwdBRrs8fdrFxdtY9eqFlpPES_YwlJcR9w4cOnepsMngtii1cHRMax9qt_M5e7ee2LQOA2YVcpUEi3Sy0=&c=fNsz3YksPHP3FUYTzAyI0CAVP_5cOyjcWrlJgzKkBE3HmdCTWcAP0w==&ch=N3tBsEHiLzUduDtApgi17KiLxelN9NQKWkKNj3woXYVs8P5cojf0bg==)

| Peter,
On Election Day, the phones at Louisiana Democratic Party headquarters in Baton Rouge started ringing at 6 a.m. and never stopped.
Hundreds of calls flooded our voter protection hotline from across the state during last Saturday's primary elections. The calls described the same story over and over: requesting a Democratic ballot but receiving a Republican ballot, voters unable to cast a ballot in the Senate primary, No Party voters receiving the incorrect forms to fill out, and many voters leaving polling locations altogether because they were so frustrated with the process.
This chaos was not an accident. As one LSU political scientist put it, Governor Landry created a system that was "almost designed in a lab to discourage people from participating in the electoral process." Our own executive director Dadrius Lanus called it what it was: voter suppression and voter intimidation.
This is what MAGA control of Louisiana elections looks like.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LK9LNBKxC5PJmZtk9Qvhk3S0ZCL5-fzoodDygO4EHy9FgQ-U1qBfvA9X0x1Yl0VbIFI3Oc9gOI4YR7JfRsdml-FnnTSvDAyj1Bg_Xja6zusFq-ReUkqhRtrUI_IVUbqJS0S2Ce59044CDSM6wyjYbHMACiVwdBRrs8fdrFxdtY9eqFlpPES_YwlJcR9w4cOnepsMngtii1cHRMax9qt_M_VLOE_4qLRybmntmkxTqYY=&c=fNsz3YksPHP3FUYTzAyI0CAVP_5cOyjcWrlJgzKkBE3HmdCTWcAP0w==&ch=N3tBsEHiLzUduDtApgi17KiLxelN9NQKWkKNj3woXYVs8P5cojf0bg==)
---
That is exactly why we are building Organize Louisiana -- the largest voter education and turnout operation this state has ever seen. Ahead of the midterms, we will be in every corner of Louisiana educating voters on their rights, how to register, how to vote, and what to do when someone tries to stop them.
After this fiasco, we also need to expand the amount of poll watchers and volunteers on the ground who can report issues at polling locations back to our headquarters immediately on Election Day. No Louisiana voter should ever walk away from a polling place without their ballot being counted.
But we cannot do this alone. The Louisiana Democratic Party is one of the most underfunded state parties in the nation. We are asking Democrats from across the country to help us fund this unprecedented operation. That's why we're asking you today: [Can we count on you to rush a donation of $25, $10, or even just $5 to help us counter MAGA's voter suppression in Louisiana?](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LK9LNBKxC5PJmZtk9Qvhk3S0ZCL5-fzoodDygO4EHy9FgQ-U1qBfvA9X0x1Yl0VbIFI3Oc9gOI4YR7JfRsdml-FnnTSvDAyj1Bg_Xja6zusFq-ReUkqhRtrUI_IVUbqJS0S2Ce59044CDSM6wyjYbHMACiVwdBRrs8fdrFxdtY9eqFlpPES_YwlJcR9w4cOnepsMngtii1cHRMax9qt_M_Nd2-Qx98XjTyMjWXjULP8=&c=fNsz3YksPHP3FUYTzAyI0CAVP_5cOyjcWrlJgzKkBE3HmdCTWcAP0w==&ch=N3tBsEHiLzUduDtApgi17KiLxelN9NQKWkKNj3woXYVs8P5cojf0bg==)

Every week, some of y'all ask me how to talk to your Republican neighbors, friends, and family members about this race. Some of them no longer recognize their party, but might not be ready to vote for a Democrat. Some of them may be waking up to the chaos and corruption of this administration, and seeing that Tim Burchett is enabling it. They're curious about their options. And of course, some of y'all ARE our Republican neighbors, friends, and family members, and you've joined this movement because you want to see someone with a strong character and work ethic getting things done for East Tennessee in Congress. I asked him what his message would be to others in his party who feel politically homeless. Some of them no longer recognize their party, but might not be ready to vote for a Democrat. For those who are curious, I sat down with a card-carrying Republican and 3x Trump voter who is supporting my campaign. I asked him what his message would be to others in his party who feel politically homeless. I encourage you to ~. Hungry for more? This weekend, federal agents arrested a 21-year-old Pennsylvania man from the suburbs of Pittsburgh, who they say was [preparing to carry out an ISIS-inspired mass shooting](https://substack.com/redirect/5faf06c1-f096-4969-9477-14bd01b34934?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). According to prosecutors, Jonathan Hunter Kramer had repeatedly pledged allegiance to ISIS online, shared extremist propaganda, and told others that he was ready for a "mission" as soon as he could obtain a weapon. Mr Kramer obtained a semi-automatic weapon in a Walmart parking lot from another individual, then purchased 190 rounds of ammo from Dunham's Sports, bought a disposable phone, and was then arrested outside his hotel room, where the FBI found these items, 30 knives, and a note that said, "I can't live in constant Fear!" Thankfully, he was stopped by the FBI and Pennsylvania State Police before he could conduct the mass shooting he talked online about doing. He previously was arrested as a delinquent minor for a separate mass casualty plot and has a history of coordinating violence using encrypted platforms by discussing chemical poisons, drone delivery explosives, and firearm attacks. Luckily, an individual reported his behavior to law enforcement.
No doubt getting this ISIS surrogate Jonathan Hunter Kramer off the streets before he did harm this week was a good thing, but it does bring up the balance of using frontier technology, including AI, to empower law enforcement to fulfill the most sacred duty of our government - to keep our families safe - while abiding by our Constitution.
# **The Bad AI Use Case - Flock Cameras**
Benjamin Franklin, who later delivered the closing speech at the Constitutional Convention, had warned decades earlier about the tradeoff between liberty and security. In 1755, he wrote, "Those who would give up essential liberty, to purchase a little temporary safety, deserve neither liberty nor safety." While Franklin was referring to taxes at that time, imagine the Orwellian horror of knowing every time you drove your car you were being secretly recorded. That is the controversy surrounding Flock cameras, automated license-plate readers now deployed across the country. It is one thing to know that police can run your license plate. It is another to learn that cameras may be logging where your car appears, over and over again, and storing those sightings in a searchable system. The technology is bringing Americans closer to a form of pervasive surveillance long associated with more intrusive states, where the government can build a detailed record of where ordinary people go and when.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/29d5102b-667c-4cd4-bd59-ff2037a8f98d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
flock camera
Pennsylvania is now having this argument in real time. Flock cameras are already in use across the state, and the backlash has been strong enough that [Gov. Josh Shapiro has joined calls to restrict or ban them.](https://substack.com/redirect/2a0fce00-8414-4a0e-80f3-a90791ce6614?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The fight is bringing a broader concern into focus about technology giving government new powers faster than the rules governing those powers can keep up. The cameras record license plates along with details about passing vehicles, including when and where they were seen, creating a searchable record of a car's movements. More than 120,000 Flock cameras are deployed nationally, according to the company, while thousands of automated license-plate readers have been identified across Pennsylvania.
At an AI summit in Pittsburgh last Thursday, [Shapiro called for federal regulation of AI,](https://substack.com/redirect/02675143-96bc-4870-b582-3de3260d7d80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) comparing it to the safety standards imposed on pharmaceuticals and commercial aviation.
Police departments argue that this kind of network can help locate stolen cars, identify suspects, and solve crimes more quickly. Civil-liberties advocates worry that the same infrastructure can create an enormous record of innocent people's movements without them ever knowing they entered a database.
Shapiro sided with the skeptics. "This is not something in the public interest," he said, while making clear that law enforcement still needs effective tools to keep communities safe.
This past weekend, Governor Shapiro weighed in on an even larger AI debate after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned about the risks posed by increasingly powerful systems. Shapiro called the warning a "bright red flashing light" for Washington and argued that development of the technology should not be left entirely to private companies.
Taken together, the two episodes capture where the politics of AI is heading.
For years, much of the AI debate focused on what the technology might someday become. Pennsylvania is confronting the more immediate problem of what happens when AI enters institutions that already hold enormous amounts of information and power.
AI now describes such a wide range of technology that the term can obscure more than it explains. A camera network that creates a searchable record of people's movements raises very different concerns from software that helps a detective search hundreds of hours of body-camera footage.
The better way to judge these systems is by what they actually allow government to do. Do they create new surveillance powers, make consequential decisions on their own, or help human beings work more efficiently with information they already possess?
Flock makes the distinction easy to see. A license-plate reader is not especially remarkable on its own. Once thousands of cameras continuously record vehicles and those sightings become searchable across jurisdictions, the scale changes the nature of the power.
A tool that might be perfectly reasonable in one investigation can become something different when it produces a historical record of everyone's movements.
This is also why it would be a mistake to treat every use of AI in law enforcement as another version of Flock.
# **Good Use of AI in Law Enforcement**
Federal prisons already generate an enormous amount of recorded phone traffic that law enforcement is legally allowed to review. In practice, that can mean asking someone to sit through hundreds of hours of calls, listening for the few minutes that may actually matter to an investigation or prosecution. It is tedious work, and not exactly the kind of job people are lining up to do.
This is the kind of problem [Flash AI ](https://substack.com/redirect/a8cb8b63-fa3e-4d40-8d75-e07df79f9747?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)is built to solve. The Ohio company uses AI to search and analyze evidence investigators already lawfully possess, including jail calls, body-camera footage, witness interviews, documents and phone extractions. Instead of replacing the investigator, the software helps narrow a mountain of material into the pieces that deserve human attention. In an Ohio statewide corrections deployment that has been running for more than three months, the company says the system has processed more than 300 million minutes of inmate call audio. Whitehall Police Department has separately reported an average reduction of roughly 80% in caseload time, literally saving days of man-hours to just hours utilizing their technology.
That makes it fundamentally different from the Flock surveillance system that is constantly collecting new information about people who are suspected of nothing. Flash is designed to help investigators understand an existing case more quickly while keeping its conclusions traceable back to the original evidence, which is a more ethical model for AI because it makes government more capable without giving it a new power to watch the public.
That does not remove the need for scrutiny, but it gives us a better standard for judging AI: whether it helps people do their jobs more effectively while preserving human accountability, limiting unnecessary surveillance, and abiding by our constitutional protections under the Bill of Rights.
I have become wary of technological debates that begin with the name of the technology rather than the power being exercised. The invention of a new tool does not repeal old democratic principles. Government should still have to justify searches and, in most cases, have to get court approval. Evidence should still be reviewable. Trial decisions and rules of evidence must still have accountable human beings behind them. Citizens should still know when the state acquires powers that would have been unimaginable a generation ago.
At the same time, government cannot reasonably respond to every new technology by delaying thoughtful implementation. We must understand that law enforcement executes the most sacred duty of government - keeping our families safe.
Police departments confront enormous amounts of digital evidence. Body cameras alone can generate hours of footage from a single incident. Investigators may have phone records, videos, documents, audio files and interviews scattered across different systems. There is a legitimate public interest in giving professionals tools that let them find relevant evidence faster, especially when those tools make the reasoning more transparent rather than less.
This is where the next stage of AI policy becomes harder and, I think, much more useful.
The goal should be to get the benefits of new technology without giving institutions powers that outrun the rules meant to govern them. Sometimes that will mean rejecting a particular use. In other cases, it will mean allowing the technology with clear limits on data, access and human review.
# **Promises Made, Promises Kept**
Pennsylvania may be stumbling toward that framework in real time.
One and a half years after Governor Shapiro and his family were assaulted in their home by a domestic terrorist, he got it right when he publicly thanked the FBI and the PA State Police last Last tuesday, Shapiro [posted to X](https://substack.com/redirect/94f163d6-5dd3-44df-9a62-394e20aa3b4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) expressing his gratitude to the FBI and Pennsylvania State Police for their swift action.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a846525a-da01-46c1-a4d3-0e2acb99674e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As someone who comes from a law enforcement family, proudly served as a federal and military prosecutor, and chaired Governor Shapiro's Public Safety Transition Team, I'm proud of his work putting more cops on the street, including funding 16 more state police cadet classes totalling 1600 new troopers, and his 'smart on crime' approach including creating the Pennsylvania Violence Research Center for evidence-based community violence intervention (CVI) programs. In politics, there are workhorses and showhorses, Shapiro is a workhorse, so I was honored to sign my name to this flyer by Kennedy Democrats:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c0fb315-7bc9-4f66-8be1-3349ee60b22c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But as a prosecutor and former constitutional law professor, I also appreciate Shapiro's positions threading the needle with balance, his correct stance on Flock cameras and empowering law enforcement when appropriate by utilizing frontier AI technology, which on the outside can look like separate news stories, but they are really part of the same political and constitutional question. Americans are becoming less interested in whether artificial intelligence is exciting or frightening in the abstract. They want to know what happens when it enters the government that already has the power to police, regulate and make decisions about their lives.
While Congress has been stagnant with AI - debating whether there should be an AI Special Committee - and President Trump suggesting an 'AI Force' modeled after the Space Force but appointing an AI Czar, he has largely dismissed calls for increased regulation, even while technologists like Elon Musk have said there's a 10-20% risk that advanced AI could be the end of human extinction.
Who is watching? What is being recorded? What is the machine deciding? Can somebody explain how it reached that conclusion? Is there an outside entity like the courts reviewing these decisions? And when something goes wrong, who answers for it?
Those are not anti-technology questions. They are the questions a democracy is supposed to ask whenever somebody acquires a new form of power.
Artificial intelligence is arriving faster than our rules for governing it.
We can still do something about it by keeping our families safe while abiding by our Constitution - Ben Franklin wouldn't want it any other way - but Congress can't continue to punt on their consequential issue of our lifetime.

| Dear Peter,

In recent weeks, more than 4 brave women — patients and providers — have taken legal action with the Center for Reproductive Rights and courageously shared their personal stories to fight back against the abortion bans that caused them unthinkable trauma.

[Since _Roe v. Wade_ was overturned, the Center has led landmark cases in Texas, Tennessee, and Idaho.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139668726/648113123/-254760887?sourceid=1151601&utm_campaign=27emage-0906aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGFkZjczZi1mNGI1LWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3cC2ZjTsog2WN80YEOdcTIXZqOOmqs--77jPAybv1E4=&emci=643412ce-0db2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=88adf73f-f4b5-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237) And we know countless others across the country have faced the same dangerous, heartbreaking experiences. The stories from these women are just the tip of the iceberg. | [Send Your Thanks](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139668727/648113124/-254760887?sourceid=1151601&utm_campaign=27emage-0906aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGFkZjczZi1mNGI1LWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3cC2ZjTsog2WN80YEOdcTIXZqOOmqs--77jPAybv1E4=&emci=643412ce-0db2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=88adf73f-f4b5-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)
---
These women are now reliving their trauma in the media and in court. No one should have to do that, but they are — to save others from the same fate, and to hold their states accountable for the suffering these laws are causing.

Texas, Oklahoma, Idaho, Tennessee, and many other states hostile toward abortion care have shown again and again that they will do anything to preserve their shameful abortion bans — even if it means putting women's lives at risk.

[Join us in thanking these brave women for their courage in fighting abortion bans.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139668728/648113125/-254760887?sourceid=1151601&utm_campaign=27emage-0906aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGFkZjczZi1mNGI1LWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3cC2ZjTsog2WN80YEOdcTIXZqOOmqs--77jPAybv1E4=&emci=643412ce-0db2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=88adf73f-f4b5-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)

Nancy Northup

Dear Patriot, **In just days, we're taking our message straight to the Library of Congress.** On September 26, I will kick off this year's "See You at the Library" Story Hours at America's Library in Washington, D.C.Then, just one week later, something truly incredible will happen. Christian parents and grandparents across America will walk into their local public libraries with their children and grandchildren.And in a matter of hours, hundreds of Story Hours will fill children's hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God.This is our chance to bring God's truth into libraries across America and reach an entire generation of children. **This year, honoring America's 250th birthday, our ambitious goal is to expand "See You at the Library Day" to reach 250,000 children.****And we are just days away.** Before then, I need you!The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host "Story Hours" has been overwhelming.But it's going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold "Story Hours" for 250,000 children.**And with just days left, the clock is running out to fund the Story Hours we need to reach 250,000 children.** **[That's why I'm asking you to rush back your tax-deductible sponsorship gift of $35, $50, $125, $250 or more today.](https://links.conservative-usa.com/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=f14df7a899ba470295fd8dc9ec51706b&_e=CWFIbNg6RpFr9Vy2Xwf81qXW2tjnk7fsYg_3rHEdwtJZblgDappzIUxmQ0ZVT-LIBZ6z8cdGi77Il3YCSA7jP-4EF2LRKJaBIswW0Q-hKdX6pnhDm8aTYeBW3NNw4BGb8nALrL5uVJZSxyQiuNzoLdYQ49JJDwGYUth55E5PPBMpYfDsjV9sPO52Ff6B_sJwss8Uy2wNR2bqrdbSrv8mbXrx5ToUgzOFW2T1PUqTVg482-q8WQC4ICRR2MTru6W6GjqeQIu438xleaC_UL90hrp_RIAUOaFgmCtscMZuh08Vl7io3apgsGXXYhfxVwxzVIEktYtMwVc41sspe-hFcmy-8Zzi3AO1b9WJiZ4C6OyVZfWQFh_HKxce3xHOFPu3tzzrXjLX-KxSTqWkKNoQCzGXmJrj2-2Usw6bLxiWogfq5iPX0QYW3DK261aqPokwMkQxeTAovXeeBniB6s9Oaxs6oGsyS3EtdNYok3dAScwMfIglOY9Ykec35nHUDRXgyeCuciHpsG350GZ0mBwEJfAyFCVgTFAW7DbmTv8f8lRqrWfozbzPhxqR_uqdQSd8GxvDWYO45cb2fZAu-r98VzffvkyE_lV3GFaPBARNKxFiPefFMyOgudNAVm22ofCofysVe-Ok8zDJqQoD4KH4mYHi49YIm8-FF3tYQ0P0t-c5lESOhg4u419IEj74sA2z)** Friend, America's children need to hear our message because today's "educators" and librarians are radicals! Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian.She would fill your mind with classics like Pat the Bunny and The Little Engine That Could.But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, radical activists have worked to turn our public libraries into vehicles for their values.But we can't just sit back and complain about it. **[That's why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through "See You at the Library Day."](https://links.conservative-usa.com/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=f14df7a899ba470295fd8dc9ec51706b&_e=CWFIbNg6RpFr9Vy2Xwf81qXW2tjnk7fsYg_3rHEdwtJZblgDappzIUxmQ0ZVT-LIBZ6z8cdGi77Il3YCSA7jP-4EF2LRKJaBIswW0Q-hKdX6pnhDm8aTYeBW3NNw4BGb8nALrL5uVJZSxyQiuNzoLdYQ49JJDwGYUth55E5PPBMpYfDsjV9sPO52Ff6B_sJwss8Uy2wNR2bqrdbSrv8mbXrx5ToUgzOFW2T1PUqTVg7QAU1cty6CZP9iaLMGXbYW1nP3PAFK0yeCO3FShSY86oNbFbkVJ1iJScksEWMSB1tMqprsrPMcRFWEEJh9IesSVk5ayhrnzchP_YwZOXNjevrpKc4abuiWKbilWwvXyk9ZKAlhoqt5f9lNy9R00NiQSDs-zVSPS_wmcmra3vWJ3GNZGUHKMo2zj7RsDiMC4IKxZ8_qhX5XfLTPVYlFQ1LxgZAOCfNXJQ3gk0-Q-zspgC7xlnZHp6Es5AIxnCCPTrjltt1WJbmbFG0csmI3NZtZ9z9X052DyTFFAobCuK8dqB7HiY9SzRc44BcIMGN7NdtnctXJzvhKTV3ZjI4VMUyEv3IVDVL8u92zMdo344wYD2tP9JzWJnEE2SmuJ6fM7tcYvedercH0ug5HfgO7nv45K0wSKzZLgbw2d6z9ZCzmE4XZc7XbnuaJrU5xUwubgHzeFjaMnG4Kiw_BlZluvT8n)** We're countering those awful "Drag Queen Story Hours" with conservative Story Hours filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism.And on October 3, a little boy or girl will stand up at their public library as straight and tall as they possibly can... ...as their right hand covers their heart, and they proudly pledge allegiance to our American flag.We'll teach them:**Freedom Requires Courage.****Great Blessings Require Great Sacrifice.****IN GOD WE TRUST.** And we hope to body:
I’ll stop sending these emails when we win the power to not need them anymore.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260921-1&t=1&akid=4043%2E587540%2EQNnvw_)
Hey Peter, David here.
Yes. This is _another_ political fundraising email.
And no, I’m not sitting here thinking, _“Yay! We get to send Peter another email!”_
I know these can feel overwhelming. So the fact that you actually open these emails, read them, and when you’re able to, you even chip in a few dollars? That means the world to me.
Because right now, **emails like these are one of the only real tools we have to raise the resources needed to build the next generation of progressive leadership.**
We don't have corporate PACs. We don’t have lobbyists. We don’t have the Democratic Party machine backing us.
But we have _you_. We have _people_. And sometimes that means we show up in your inbox more than either of us would prefer.
But I promise you this, Peter:
**The day young progressive leaders finally have a real seat at the table, these emails _stop_.** The day we aren’t fighting uphill for representation and change? I will _gladly_ stop emailing you. Honestly, my hope is that one day our candidates reform the campaign finance system enough that elections are won by who the best organizer is, not who can raise the most money.
But we’re not there yet. And until we are, we have work to do — and we simply can’t do it without grassroots support from people like you.
We’re solving the chicken-and-egg problem that keeps our political system so broken. The problem being that if we are going to change laws, we need morally just leaders who don’t take corporate money. The other problem, though, is that it’s very hard to build power without taking money from special interests like private utilities or big pharma.
That’s where you come in. We need thousands of small-dollar donors to help grow the power of our candidates so they can take on those special interests without taking money from them.
We’re up against entrenched, powerful interests designed to keep things exactly as they are. Electing bold, young progressives who want to _actually change things_? That makes a lot of powerful people _really_ uncomfortable. And that’s exactly why Leaders We Deserve exists and why we’re so powerful.
And your support fuels this fight. And yes, sometimes that means more emails than you might like. It’s not because we expect you to give every time — but because when you can, _it matters_. The ripple effect is real. **A thousand small actions add up to generational change.**
So Peter, if you’re in a position to do so today, we’d be grateful.
**[Chip in $5 to help us build the future we deserve.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260921_1_resendemails.aHWwIy&refcode=em20260921-4043&amount=5&t=2&akid=4043%2E587540%2EQNnvw_)**

One day, when we win the power we’re building towards, your inbox will be _a lot_ quieter.
And our future will be _a lot_ better.
Thank you for your support.
David Hogg

But I promise you this, Peter: The day young progressive leaders finally have a real seat at the table, these emails stop. The day we aren’t fighting uphill for representation and change? I will gladly stop emailing you. Honestly, my hope is that one day our candidates reform the campaign finance system enough that elections are won by who the best organizer is, not who can raise the most money. But we’re not there yet. And until we are, we have work to do — and we simply can’t do it without grassroots support from people like you. We’re solving the chicken-and-egg problem that keeps our political system so broken. The problem being that if we are going to change laws, we need morally just leaders who don’t take corporate money. The other problem, though, is that it’s very hard to build power without taking money from special interests like private utilities or big pharma. That’s where you come in. We need thousands of small-dollar donors to help grow the power of our candidates so they can take on those special interests without taking money from them. We’re up against entrenched, powerful interests designed to keep things exactly as they are. Electing bold, young progressives who want to actually change things? That makes a lot of powerful people really uncomfortable. And that’s exactly why Leaders We Deserve exists and why we’re so powerful. And your support fuels this fight. And yes, sometimes that means more emails than you might like. It’s not because we expect you to give every time — but because when you can, it matters. The ripple effect is real. A thousand small actions add up to generational change. So Peter, if you’re in a position to do so today, we’d be grateful. One day, when we win the power we’re building towards, your inbox will be a lot quieter. And our future will be a lot better. Thank you for your support. David Hogg

clean_body: | | Peter, Today's message is a longer one, but this is important. I'm writing to share with you details about the latest shooting by ICE agents in Texas and the fast expanding pattern of violence at the hands of this agency. Yesterday afternoon in North Austin, an ICE agent shot a man in the middle of a DoorDash delivery. His name is Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, and what happened is a tragedy. And worse: the hospital refused to let his wife see him. Instead he was turned over to ICE agents after just 9 hours of medical treatment, and moved to an undisclosed location. As I write this, his family reportedly still does not know where he is OR his condition. Reports from the scene detail a blue Corolla full of bullet holes, as many as five shots fired, and multiple torso wounds in the victim. | The facts are still coming in, but one thing is clear: an independent investigation is needed, immediately. DHS spent last night doing what it always does after its agents shoot somebody, polishing an official account that clears DHS of everything. Look at the record in Texas alone. Wilber is the third person shot by federal immigration agents in this state under this administration. They killed an American citizen on South Padre Island. They killed a 52-year-old Houston man with no criminal record in this state, then jailed the witness to that shooting for weeks. Days ago, federal agents beat and pepper-sprayed two Texas teenagers who were on their way to enlist in the Marines. | Nobody has answered for any of it. ICE is a rogue agency that has terrorized the whole country, but it has built its headquarters of misery right here in Texas. Our state cages more of their detainees than any other, spread across 23 facilities, and at least 14 human beings have died in Texas custody since 2025. At the Fort Bliss camp outside El Paso, the largest detention site in America, inspectors logged 49 violations, including staff failing to run the checks that prevent suicides. I have stood with the wives and families of the wrongfully deported and listened to how this agency has ruined their lives. There is no other option left: Texans will root this cruelty out of our state, and I will help lead that fight. This violent machine runs on total impunity, because bigoted men like Keith Self shield it in Washington while Greg Abbott runs interference in Austin. When Democrats retake the majority, there must be a full investigation into every one of these incidents, and accountability for the abuses and the coverups alike. My service to this country did not end when I hung up my uniform. I did not bury brothers and sisters in arms so that an abusive government agency could wreak terror on the freedoms they died defending. clean_body: Peter, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. That's about 75 doors and 25 real conversations with voters who haven't made up their minds yet, and who deserve to hear from us before it's too late. Friend, _We've heard it before._ When Tennesseans _call on their leaders_ to address the high cost of gas and groceries, soaring medical debt, and making sure our kids have every advantage to succeed, _**they say “We’d love to do all that, but we’ll have to raise taxes to pay fior it.”**_ __ They’d have us think we either _settle_ for underfunded classrooms, crushing medical debt, delapedated infrustructure, or pay higher taxes to fix it. _**Well, we're calling bull.**_ **_We don't need to raise your taxes by a single penny to build a stronger Tennessee._** We just need to stop playing political games with the money we already have and start putting it to work for working families. That is what our campaign is all about. **Look at what we will do— _without raising your taxes:_**
* **Wipe Out Medical & Housing Debt:** Use state funds to wipe out predatory medical debt for over 100,000 Tennesseans and help working families secure affordable housing by tackling security deposits head-on.
* **Fully Fund Our Public Classrooms:** Invest in universal pre-K, raise teacher pay, and restore respect to the profession—ensuring our small towns and rural schools aren't left behind to fund private school vouchers.
* **Expand Rural Healthcare: **Broaden Medicaid access to keep our rural hospitals open, protect reproductive freedom, and lower prescription drug costs so families aren't forced to choose between health and bankruptcy.
* **Keep the TVA Public & Protect Our Land: **Sign an Executive Order to keep the Tennessee Valley Authority a public utility serving the people—not corporate profits—while protecting our clean air, water, and farmlands from overdevelopment.

clean_body: | Friend, We've heard it before. When Tennesseans call on their leaders to address the high cost of gas and groceries, soaring medical debt, and making sure our kids have every advantage to succeed, they say “We’d love to do all that, but we’ll have to raise taxes to pay fior it.” They’d have us think we either settle for underfunded classrooms, crushing medical debt, delapedated infrustructure, or pay higher taxes to fix it. Well, we're calling bull. We don't need to raise your taxes by a single penny to build a stronger Tennessee. We just need to stop playing political games with the money we already have and start putting it to work for working families. That is what our campaign is all about. Look at what we will do— without raising your taxes: Wipe Out Medical & Housing Debt: Use state funds to wipe out predatory medical debt for over 100,000 Tennesseans and help working families secure affordable housing by tackling security deposits head-on. Fully Fund Our Public Classrooms: Invest in universal pre-K, raise teacher pay, and restore respect to the profession—ensuring our small towns and rural schools aren't left behind to fund private school vouchers. Expand Rural Healthcare: Broaden Medicaid access to keep our rural hospitals open, protect reproductive freedom, and lower prescription drug costs so families aren't forced to choose between health and bankruptcy. Keep the TVA Public & Protect Our Land: Sign an Executive Order to keep the Tennessee Valley Authority a public utility serving the people—not corporate profits—while protecting our clean air, water, and farmlands from overdevelopment. Anyone trying to sell you the false choice between a good quality of life and higher taxes is looking out for special interests, not everyday Tennesseans. If you believe it's time to elect a governor that will tell the truth about taxes and fight for everyday Tennesseans , our movement, and sign-up to , and help us take back Tennessee, without raising your taxes! | | = | | Tennesseans don't have to settle for false chices.We are building a Tennessee that actually works for everybody, together. Peter,

It’s Congresswoman Analilia Mejia.

# **Cantor** Fitzgerald**just priced Securitize like Wall Street 's onchain toll booth**
Cantor Fitzgerald slapped an Overweight and a $21.20 target on Securitize, calling 95% upside from Friday's $10.86 close. The stock jumped 9.4% on the note after the SEC's Thursday rule let limited U.S. tokenized stocks trade. $5 billion onchain today. $319 trillion still sitting in the old vault. That's not a product. That's a land grab.
* **Winners?** Securitize, Cantor's clients who get the regulated full stack, and whoever owns the rails when stocks start settling like crypto.
* **Losers?** Unregulated tokenization shops and transfer-agent fossils. If the world wants one roof for issue, register, custody, distribute, and trade, the cowboys get boxed out.
* **Next?** Watch volume under that temporary SEC rule. If tokenized names actually trade, $21.20 is the opening bid, not the dream. If it's theater, this $1.8 billion toy snaps back.

Gacetta said tokenization is the biggest financial-infrastructure overhaul in a century and Securitize covers the whole lifecycle. Cute line. The only number that matters is 0.01% of $319 trillion already onchain. That's greenfield. Just don't confuse a $21 target on a money-losing $14 million-revenue shop with a done deal. Rails first. Revenue later.

# **Bitcoin cleared $85k because Congress failed and the SEC refused to wait**
Bitcoin punched through $85,375.50, up 6.03%, the first print above $85k since January. The Clarity Act died in the Senate last week. Michael Saylor called the corpse a win. Strategy bought $75.7 million of coin and $174 million of its own preferred. Thursday the SEC green-lit limited tokenized-stock trading anyway.
* **Winners?** Saylor, Strategy, Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle, and Fidelity's FBTC inflows. Anyone long bitcoin above the $80,500 corporate-treasury cost basis just got paid.
* **Losers?** Community banks that killed stablecoin holding rewards and still lost the tape. Shorts who ate $740 million of liquidations. Senate Democrats who handed the narrative to Atkins.
* **Next?** Spot ETF cost basis sits at $85,638. Clear it and the magnet is the mid-January $97k high. Fed speak is the only near-term landmine this week.

On Sep. 3 in **["Atkins just paved the Crypto onshore path Gensler spent four years blocking,"](https://substack.com/redirect/a9f57f19-4f07-4c41-bcec-d4fb76880b85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I said if Congress stalls, Atkins moves anyway. He did. On Aug. 20 in **["Trump's crypto team writes the rules while Congress stalls,"](https://substack.com/redirect/e2fbb37b-110e-48aa-a35b-787c65dd0c46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I said executive action fills the vacuum. Bitcoin just collected both bets in cash.

# **Muse just handed Zuck the receipt Wall Street demanded**
Meta ripped about 12% to $744 Monday after Muse parked itself at No. 1 on Apple's U.S. App Store. Wells Fargo jacked the target from $640 to $796 two days before Connect. Two weeks after the Sept. 8 launch the agent is booking dinners and arguing with merchants. Capex skeptics just got their faces ripped off.
* **Winners?** Zuckerberg, META holders, and every shop selling him silicon and power. The $145 billion spend finally has a consumer product people actually tap.
* **Losers?** OpenAI, Anthropic, and every analyst who called Muse vapor. Three billion daily users plus cheap in-house models is a distribution nuke they cannot match.
* **Next?** Wednesday's Connect is the exam. Retention, paid-tier conversion, and any glasses hook decide if $796 is the floor or the fade. No product metrics, no mercy.

**[I called this on Jul 10](https://substack.com/redirect/ba367f4d-01e3-44d0-97bc-d5d1a52d3a1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** when I said the monetization plan would shove it toward $700 fast. It cleared $744 today. The bears who treated capex like a crime just funded the longs' vacation.

# **Lisa Su just kicked AMD through the $1 trillion door**
AMD briefly cleared a $1 trillion market cap for the first time and the tape didn't blink. Shares ripped to $613.92, up about 9% Monday and 24% in five sessions, after a year that already delivered more than 180%. This is the AI hardware trade coming back from the dead. Lisa Su is no longer selling chips. She's selling the whole damn rack.
* **Winners?** AMD holders, Lisa Su, and every SOX name that survived the summer flush. Intel tagging along +11% is the tell that inference CPUs still print cash.
* **Losers?** Anyone still short the "AI capex hangover" story. Nvidia's $5.4 trillion throne is safe, but the monopoly premium just got a $1 trillion rival.
* **Next?** Money chases systems, not slideshows. Su guided data-center sales to double in 2027. If Connect-week Muse demand stays hot, this breakout doesn't fade.

I **[flagged the setup](https://substack.com/redirect/9db0e1e4-1ffe-44f2-aafc-2260207058a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** when SOX kissed 11,950 and I said defend that floor or get carried out. The bounce is here, SOX ~12,366. **[Micron already crashed the $1 trillion party.](https://substack.com/redirect/ed0a1b33-c59c-4f3a-a189-a3873eb81c10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** AMD just RSVP'd.

# **Grail rips 35% after the FDA staff stopped hunting for a kill shot**
Grail detonated about 35% to roughly $110 after FDA staff posted briefing docs that refused to bury Galleri. No major concerns on accuracy. No major concerns on safety. Wednesday's advisory panel still has to vote, but the staff just took the easy "this thing is junk" argument off the table. That's why the stock went vertical.
* **Winners?** Grail longs who bought the February UK-trial wreckage. Piper Sandler's David Westenberg called the docs constructive and expects a favorable vote.
* **Losers?** Skeptics who treated one messy UK trial as a death certificate. Also every payer still pretending a 50-cancer blood test isn't coming for coverage rules.
* **Next?** Wednesday's panel is the real tell. Staff already waved through performance and safety. The fight is whether they can call it "early detection."

Galleri already booked $136.8 million in 2025 U.S. sales as a lab test nobody's insurer wants to touch. FDA ink turns that into Medicare scale. The UK miss crushed this name more than 20% since February. Today's rip prices the chance Washington just blinked. Don't confuse a staff memo with approval. Don't fade a 35% bid either.
* * *
* * *
# **Trump priced Canadian potash on Truth Social and the fertilizer tape folded**
Trump posted before 11 a.m. that Washington is working a massive Belarus potash deal priced substantially less than Canada. Nutrien, Mosaic, CF Industries, and Intrepid Potash all hit session lows. Canada still supplies about 80% of U.S. farm potash. Lukashenko already said 2026 tonnes are spoken for. This is a trade-war headline, not a cargo at the dock.
* **Winners?** U.S. farmers if a real discount cargo ever lands. Trump gets a club to swing at Ottawa. Lukashenko gets another photo after the March sanctions lift.
* **Losers?** Nutrien, Mosaic, and Intrepid. Saskatchewan just became a political hostage. CF got tagged even though it sells nitrogen, not potash.
* **Next?** Demand a price, a volume, and a port that is not Klaipeda under EU sanctions. No contract means this dip is a rumor tax. Watch the bounce.

The Street sold first, which is what you do when a President marks your commodity on social media. Then the names bounced because nobody produced terms. Nutrien's own math: every $25 a tonne in potash is $280 million of EBITDA. Until Minsk names a vessel, this is noise with a 4% drawdown stapled to it.
* * *
* * *
# **Greenland 's security pact juiced the junior miners before a single shovel moved**
Monday treated a Friday security pact like a mining permit. Critical Metals ripped 37.5% to $9.22. Greenland Energy jumped as much as 159%. Greenland Mines printed a double. The deal is military basing, adversary lockout, and a UNGA signature this week. Tanbreez still does not pour first ore until late 2028.
* **Winners?** CRML, GLND, and GRML holders who sell this spike. Defense contractors who actually pour concrete. Western rare-earth longs trading the China-hedge headline.
* **Losers?** Late money buying a 2029 concentrate story at Monday's print. China keeps the processing monopoly. Greenland Energy already got warned for landing kit without permission.
* **Next?** Sign the text at UNGA. Then watch for offtake, Pentagon money, or a real permit. REMX already gave back about 40% from the June peak.

Tanbreez holds about 45 million metric tons and 27% heavy rare earths. That is a real deposit. It is also a late-2028 science project. The West needed these metals yesterday. A Truth Social FOREVER post does not move a tonne of concentrate. Take the rip. Do not marry the junior.
* * *
* * *
# That's the tape.
Securitize is a toll booth with a $21 dream attached. Bitcoin collected the Atkins call in cash. Muse is the receipt. AMD is the club. Grail is a bet on Wednesday. Belarus potash is a rumor with a drawdown. Greenland is a 2028 science project wearing a 37% costume.
Now get back to work.

Capex skeptics just got their faces ripped off. Winners? Zuckerberg, META holders, and every shop selling him silicon and power. The $145 billion spend finally has a consumer product people actually tap. Losers? OpenAI, Anthropic, and every analyst who called Muse vapor. Three billion daily users plus cheap in-house models is a distribution nuke they cannot match. Next? Wednesday's Connect is the exam. Retention, paid-tier conversion, and any glasses hook decide if $796 is the floor or the fade. No product metrics, no mercy. when I said the monetization plan would shove it toward $700 fast. It cleared $744 today. The bears who treated capex like a crime just funded the longs' vacation. Lisa Su just kicked AMD through the $1 trillion door AMD briefly cleared a $1 trillion market cap for the first time and the tape didn't blink. Shares ripped to $613.92, up about 9% Monday and 24% in five sessions, after a year that already delivered more than 180%. This is the AI hardware trade coming back from the dead. Lisa Su is no longer selling chips. She's selling the whole damn rack. Winners? AMD holders, Lisa Su, and every SOX name that survived the summer flush. Intel tagging along +11% is the tell that inference CPUs still print cash. Losers? Anyone still short the "AI capex hangover" story. Nvidia's $5.4 trillion throne is safe, but the monopoly premium just got a $1 trillion rival. Next? Money chases systems, not slideshows. Su guided data-center sales to double in 2027. If Connect-week Muse demand stays hot, this breakout doesn't fade. I when SOX kissed 11,950 and I said defend that floor or get carried out. The bounce is here, SOX ~12,366. AMD just RSVP'd. The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! Grail rips 35% after the FDA staff stopped hunting for a kill shot Grail detonated about 35% to roughly $110 after FDA staff posted briefing docs that refused to bury Galleri. No major concerns on accuracy. No major concerns on safety. Wednesday's advisory panel still has to vote, but the staff just took the easy "this thing is junk" argument off the table. That's why the stock went vertical. Winners? Grail longs who bought the February UK-trial wreckage. Piper Sandler's David Westenberg called the docs constructive and expects a favorable vote. Losers? Skeptics who treated one messy UK trial as a death certificate. Also every payer still pretending a 50-cancer blood test isn't coming for coverage rules. Next? Wednesday's panel is the real tell. Staff already waved through performance and safety. The fight is whether they can call it "early detection." Galleri already booked $136.8 million in 2025 U.S. sales as a lab test nobody's insurer wants to touch. FDA ink turns that into Medicare scale. The UK miss crushed this name more than 20% since February. Today's rip prices the chance Washington just blinked. Don't confuse a staff memo with approval. Don't fade a 35% bid either. Trump priced Canadian potash on Truth Social and the fertilizer tape folded Trump posted before 11 a.m. that Washington is working a massive Belarus potash deal priced substantially less than Canada. Nutrien, Mosaic, CF Industries, and Intrepid Potash all hit session lows. Canada still supplies about 80% of U.S. farm potash. Lukashenko already said 2026 tonnes are spoken for. This is a trade-war headline, not a cargo at the dock. Winners? U.S. farmers if a real discount cargo ever lands. Trump gets a club to swing at Ottawa. Lukashenko gets another photo after the March sanctions lift. Losers? Nutrien, Mosaic, and Intrepid. Saskatchewan just became a political hostage. CF got tagged even though it sells nitrogen, not potash. Next? Demand a price, a volume, and a port that is not Klaipeda under EU sanctions. No contract means this dip is a rumor tax. At least five Israeli-backed Palestinian militias are operating out of compounds in areas under Israeli military control across the Gaza Strip. Source: Forensic Architecture.
At least five Israeli-backed Palestinian militias are operating out of compounds in areas under Israeli military control across the Gaza Strip, according to satellite imagery and videos published online. Since the so-called ceasefire went into effect nearly a year ago, these compounds have been upgraded and expanded in size and sophistication, according to a preliminary analysis by Forensic Architecture. Many of these upgrades resemble Israeli military infrastructure, with berms, barracks, fences, and buildings. At least one compound in East Rafah includes new shops, classrooms, and a playground.
While there have been some splinter groups and defections, the five main Israel-backed Palestinian militias are known as:
* Northern forces/Popular Army in Beit Lahia, led by Ashraf Al-Mansi
* Popular Defense Forces in Shujaieya, east of Gaza City, led by Rami Halas
* Free Homeland Forces in central/eastern Gaza near Deir al-Balah, led by Shawqi Abu Nasira
* Counter-Terrorism Strike Force in southeastern Khan Younis, led by Hussam al-Astal
* Popular Forces/Counter-Terrorism Service in East Rafah, led by Ghassan Al-Duhaini

Many of the militia leaders who rose to power in collaboration with Israel during the genocide in Gaza are former gang leaders with a history of criminal activity, were associated with jihadi groups, or are former Palestinian Authority security forces that were all sidelined after Hamas gained control of the enclave in 2007.
"These militias are not just Israel-backed. These militias are Israel-created," Muhammad Shehada, a writer and analyst from Gaza and a visiting fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told Drop Site News. "The IDF and the Shin Bet [Israel's domestic intelligence service] were the ones that recruited, funded, trained, provided shelter, accommodation, food, and so on to these gangs, brought them together, and designated each one of them a very specific turf that they operate in."
Four of the five compounds where the militias are based are located very close to the "yellow line"--the demarcation of Israel's line of control--and all are close to Israeli military bases. Israel has established nearly 40 military bases in areas across Gaza east of the yellow line. One militia compound located in east Khan Younis, right on the yellow line, is less than one kilometer from two Israeli military bases.
Initially, Israel's primary objective for the gangs was to systematically loot aid coming into Gaza, starting around May 2024, as Israeli troops stood by and did not intervene. "That was the first use that Israel had for them: loot aid systematically while giving Israel plausible deniability," Shehada said. "They eventually dressed them up in police uniforms with Palestinian logos on to pretend that they were some sort of a legitimate authority with a propaganda psyop operation behind them." He added, "They suddenly became an organized militia instead of just bandits."
Militia members are granted relative freedom of movement by the Israeli military and privileged access to resources, such as weapons and medical treatment within Israel. Militias have also conducted armed raids and [attacks](https://substack.com/redirect/7deb6e64-3e72-4007-be64-a311b9cd0b71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Palestinians living near the yellow line in coordination with the Israeli military, who have backed them up with artillery and aerial support.
At least one compound in East Rafah includes new shops, classrooms, and a playground. A [video](https://substack.com/redirect/bf6e9f6c-9741-4c83-bad7-1e736123a719?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published on April 2, 2026 shows the inside of a classroom equipped with air conditioning inside the compound of the Counter-Terrorism Service militia. In the video, Ghassan Al-Duhaini--who took over as commander of the Popular Forces militia, also known as the Counter-Terrorism Service, following the killing of its former leader Yasser Abu Shabbab--is seen touring a classroom as schoolchildren receive educational instruction. These compounds are not open to all Palestinians but are used for a select few, including the families of those affiliated with the militias.
Since the so-called ceasefire went into effect nearly a year ago, Israel has been [fortifying](https://substack.com/redirect/e76152c6-b898-471e-8228-da8a0640bcc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) military bases in the eastern part of the territory it controls and constructing a physical barrier walling off Palestinians from most of the Gaza Strip. In parallel, the compounds for the Israel-backed Palestinian militias have also been upgraded and fortified, including using Israeli construction materials such as T walls (a T-shaped structural barrier or wall panel).
The ongoing construction and fortification of the Israeli military bases and Palestinian militia compounds comes despite a complete lack of reconstruction in the western part of Gaza, where nearly all Palestinians in Gaza have been corralled. Israel has not allowed reconstruction materials and equipment into Gaza over the past year, in violation of the ceasefire agreement. Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians are living in dilapidated tent encampments or seeking shelter in buildings badly damaged by the Israeli assault that are at risk of collapse. Last week, in just the latest incident, at least 21 Palestinians, including 12 children, were killed and 45 others injured when a residential building collapsed in Gaza City. More than 100 people, including 50 children, are estimated to have been sheltering in the building.
"The thing to know about these gangs is that their structures are entirely unsustainable," Shehada said. "They have been artificially created by the Israeli government, the army, the Shin Bet--and the only thing that binds them together is basically the bribes that they receive from the IDF, the protection that they receive from the IDF, the territory that they are allowed to live in, with upgraded privileges compared to the rest of the population in western Gaza. If these things disappear, the gangs will disintegrate."

Since the so-called ceasefire went into effect nearly a year ago, Israel has been military bases in the eastern part of the territory it controls and constructing a physical barrier walling off Palestinians from most of the Gaza Strip. In parallel, the compounds for the Israel-backed Palestinian militias have also been upgraded and fortified, including using Israeli construction materials such as T walls (a T-shaped structural barrier or wall panel). The ongoing construction and fortification of the Israeli military bases and Palestinian militia compounds comes despite a complete lack of reconstruction in the western part of Gaza, where nearly all Palestinians in Gaza have been corralled. Israel has not allowed reconstruction materials and equipment into Gaza over the past year, in violation of the ceasefire agreement. More than 100 people, including 50 children, are estimated to have been sheltering in the building. | Peter,

One of the most basic responsibilities of the government is making sure the food we buy is safe to eat.

**The Trump administration has failed to fulfill this basic responsibility.**

As a doctor, I know that protecting public health starts with prevention. That means having experienced scientists, inspectors, and public health professionals in place to identify problems early and respond quickly when threats emerge.

Trump and RFK Jr. have overseen significant staffing cuts and upheaval across federal health agencies, including the FDA and CDC. Many FDA food-safety programs were disrupted following those cuts, and food-safety experts are now warning that the loss of experienced staff make it harder to prevent, detect, and respond to foodborne illness.

**Food safety should never be a partisan issue.** Americans should be able to walk into a grocery store, buy food for their families, and trust that the federal agencies charged with protecting our food supply have the people and resources necessary to do their jobs.

**_That’s why taking back the House in November is so important. Democrats will restore oversight to Washington and hold this Administration accountable for their failures to keep our food supply safe._**

name: RPVI
subject: You're Invited — Meet the Candidates Reception, Oct 12, 2026 on St. Croix
body:
You are invited to the Meet the Candidates Cocktail Reception to open the night, followed by an Intimate Dinner with our V.I. Senate Candidates.

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/WF_sT90eS4K?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
| | | | | |
Hello,You are invited to the Meet the Candidates**Cocktail Reception** to open the night, followed by an **Intimate Dinner with our V.I. Senate Candidates.** A special evening bringing together supporters and the candidates working to restore real competition and accountability to the Virgin Islands government.The reception is hosted by RPVI Chairman John Yob, Francie Whitenburg, Jim Hughes, and Dr. Alexandria Coronado Hughes. Whether you join us for the reception, the dinner, or both, it's a rare chance to meet our slate of candidates in person, hear their vision for the islands, and stand alongside the community that's making it possible. **Meet the Candidates****Raymond T. James, Esq.** _(St. Croix District)_
A lifelong Virgin Islander and small businessman who served as Assistant Attorney General, Raymond has spent his career fighting for the people of these islands. He's running to bring real accountability, integrity, and a clear-eyed vision back to Virgin Islands government.**Eric Tillett** _(St. Thomas & St. John District)_
A builder, not a career politician. Eric is ready to restructure WAPA, modernize the grid, and drive down electric rates — while growing a digital economy so our islands are no longer dependent on tourism alone.**Derrick Callwood** _(St. Thomas & St. John District)_
Shaped by years in community organizing and law enforcement, Derrick knows what island families need: better roads, reliable power, affordable housing, and stronger public schools. He's running to deliver all four.**

Event Details

Monday, October 12
**
**Cocktail Reception:** 5:30 – 6:30 PM
An hour of cocktails and mingling with fellow supporters, connecting with old and new friends and neighbors from across the islands. Meet and greet with the candidates who are stepping up to serve the people of the VI face-to-face.
**Cocktail Reception ticket:** $50
---
| [COCKTIAL RECEPTION TICKETS](https://us.list-manage.com/iQmX8V22rbH?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
---
| |

**Intimate Dinner with VI Senate Candidates:** 6:30 PM
After the cocktail reception, the evening continues with an intimate seated dinner with the Senate candidates from across the VI. Sit down with Raymond, Eric, and Derrick. Hear their vision for the islands up close, ask the questions that matter to you, and share a memorable evening over delicious food and great company.
**Dinner Tickets** : $500
---
| [DINNER TICKETS](https://us.list-manage.com/vCgNBsk6SnS?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
---
| |

Seating is limited for the dinner, and we'd be honored to have you join us. **Tickets can be reserved using the links or at**[** RPVI.org**](https://us.list-manage.com/PtThQtO025W?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d) — simply click on "[Events](https://us.list-manage.com/Ne_zWrmZz3s?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)"
We look forward to seeing you there.Regards,
John Yob, RPVI Chairman

---
| | | | | | | | | | | [CHECK OUT RPVI.ORG](https://us.list-manage.com/W0V7Ln0BIoo?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)

That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. clean_body: Newsom signed a law to stop me The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Peter, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Peter: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Peter. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Peter, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! ---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-hamilton-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260921_9183_fr&refcode2=9183_22930333_bjGn6G&akid=9183%2E22930333%2EbjGn6G)
---
Derek,
A few weeks ago, I visited the Land of Oz museum in Liberal, Kansas.
While there, I watched a clip from the movie of Dorothy and Toto with her trusty sidekicks: The Scarecrow, who needed a brain; the Tin Man, who needed a heart; and the Cowardly Lion, who needed courage.
**Derek, I was struck by how that sums up exactly what’s wrong with Washington, D.C. right now.**
Too many politicians in Washington have lost their minds. They’re not using their critical thinking skills to solve problems. They’re not thinking for themselves or their constituents; they’re doing what their president tells them to.
Too many politicians have lost their hearts. They go to Washington and get too busy to listen to their constituents. They lose sight of why they ran for office and who they’re in D.C. to represent.
**_And too many politicians have lost the courage to stand up to the president and say no._** To refuse to vote for a bill that will take money out of the pockets of people back home and give it to billionaires. To stand up for what’s right, even if the president is going to bully you, primary you, or call you names.
**That is why we need to elect leaders who will have the heart, brains, and courage to stand up for what’s right, even when it’s hard.**
That means making massive investments in organizing, infrastructure, and turnout between now and Election Day.
Derek, the end of this month is our last end-of-quarter deadline before Election Day. That means everyone – including my opponent Sen. Marshall and his allies – will see firsthand how strong our movement is.**That FEC report tells the country something words can't. It shows how many people are standing up for something different. Something better and truer to our values.**
[**If you’re with me, I’m asking you to split a $20 donation between our campaign and the DNC today. Your contribution will help power our victory here in Kansas and beyond.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-hamilton-split?refcode=em_20260921_9183_fr&amount=20&refcode2=9183_22930333_bjGn6G&akid=9183%2E22930333%2EbjGn6G)

clean_body: Peter, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. That's about 75 doors and 25 real conversations with voters who haven't made up their minds yet, and who deserve to hear from us before it's too late. For America and for Charlie, A Turning Point PAC Arizona Ballot Chaser Paid for by Turning Point PAC Arizona. Not authorized by any candidate or agents acting on any candidate's behalf. Just weeks after joining John in Vancouver, Speaker Johnson is returning to headline a special fundraising roundtable and reception in Olympia on **Tuesday, September 29**.

His return underscores the national attention surrounding this race. Washington’s 3rd Congressional District is one of a small number of competitive seats that will determine which party controls the U.S. House next year, and national leaders are investing their time here because they know John can win this seat.
This is a unique opportunity to hear directly from **Speaker Johnson and John Braun** about the stakes in WA-03, the fight for control of Congress, and the work ahead in the final weeks before Election Day.

For the past several weeks, I have been reporting on how Communist China took [control](https://substack.com/redirect/9ca6a7c1-910b-4a07-87c5-1cd8568b5d00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Smithfield Foods, America's largest pork producer. Sadly, Smithfield is not an isolated case. It is a pattern, and the CCP is using the same playbook in the maritime industry.
Ferretti Group is a global shipbuilder behind brands like Riva, Pershing, Custom Line, and Wally. It has nearly 10% of the global luxury yacht market, and these boats visit ports across the US and Europe. Now, Ferretti is[ controlled by Weichai Group](https://substack.com/redirect/7c079681-c953-4abe-903c-a3abe8e5a363?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a Chinese state-owned conglomerate.
Weichai was founded in 1946 to make rifles for the People's Liberation Army during China's civil war. It has built tank engines for the PLA since the 1970s. Its engines power the PHL-11 rocket launcher that the blacklisted arms giant NORINCO [supplies ](https://substack.com/redirect/a20eff07-76f8-409b-865e-b48c837a457d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)to the Chinese military. Weichai's client list includes U.S.-sanctioned defense contractors like MAZ of Belarus and Kamaz of Russia, which supply Russian forces fighting in Ukraine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/027003c9-2689-4245-b079-667fc7c49a42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee0ac182-599b-4167-b6c6-46e19c45ede2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/876a4a16-c690-49cb-a166-64d2c8fa2d66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Weichai is wholly [owned](https://substack.com/redirect/623eb8b3-f6ee-4262-b599-4f80394ffebe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Shandong Heavy Industry Group, which answers to China's State-Owned Assets Supervision and Administration (SASAC), the Chinese state owned asset management commission.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/12465364-62b1-43e6-8cd1-fe99e2e958fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c8697c26-db40-44fb-9182-5aee1a830ae1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
SASAC is mentioned in the Pentagon's 1260H list a WHOPPING 74 TIMES, by far more than any other entity mentioned on the list. To get on the 1260H list, a company doesn't need to be directly owned by the Chinese government; it can merely be "affiliated" or "indirectly" owned. 21 companies on the current list are "affiliated" with SASAC and 28 are "indirectly" owned. For 9 out of the 28 indirectly owned companies, SASAC ownership was the sole basis the Department of War cited. Weichai's case is stronger than all of those because, as Sen. Jim Banks wrote in a statement, Weichai has direct ties to blacklisted Chinese military companies.
